page: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the r3-256 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block bandwidth reaching 4744.5 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 279.53 GB/sec. Database operations are a key strength, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 30782.6 and Redis SET operations executing at 75.95 million operations per second. Single-core performance, such as Geekbench single-core and gzip compression, falls within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated core allocation combined with 256 GB of RAM offers a highly cost-efficient profile for memory-bound enterprise applications. The absence of hyperthreading ensures predictable execution times for compute-heavy tasks. This server is well-suited for hosting large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
